statements.impact_statement: CVE-2023-49092 (GHSA-c38w-74pg-36hr, RUSTSEC-2023-0071): the RustCrypto rsa crate's private-key operations are not constant time, so an attacker who can measure the time of RSA decryption or signing with a private key, for example over a network, may recover the key (the Marvin Attack, https://people.redhat.com/~hkario/marvin/). RustSec lists it as fixed in rsa 0.10.0, which moves to constant-time arithmetic (https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/19, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/626). Listed the files of every published build-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (2.6.4-r0 to 2.29.1-r1, x86_64 and aarch64; 2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only). Each installs one file, /usr/bin/build, a Go program; no build contains Rust code or the rsa crate, so the vulnerable component is not present in this package.

CVE-2023-49092 (GHSA-c38w-74pg-36hr, RUSTSEC-2023-0071): the RustCrypto rsa crate's private-key operations are not constant time, so an attacker who can measure the time of RSA decryption or signing with a private key, for example over a network, may recover the key (the Marvin Attack, https://people.redhat.com/~hkario/marvin/). RustSec lists it as fixed in rsa 0.10.0, which moves to constant-time arithmetic (https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/19, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/626). Listed the files of every published build-fips-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 FIPS package repository (2.6.4-r0 to 2.29.1-r1, x86_64 and aarch64; 2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only). Each installs one file, /usr/bin/build, a Go program; no build contains Rust code or the rsa crate, so the vulnerable component is not present in this package.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2023-49092 (GHSA-c38w-74pg-36hr, RUSTSEC-2023-0071): the RustCrypto rsa crate's private-key operations are not constant time, so an attacker who can measure the time of RSA decryption or signing with a private key, for example over a network, may recover the key (the Marvin Attack, https://people.redhat.com/~hkario/marvin/). RustSec lists it as fixed in rsa 0.10.0, which moves to constant-time arithmetic (https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0071.html, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/19, https://github.com/RustCrypto/RSA/issues/626). Listed the files of every published build-fips package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 FIPS package repository (2.6.4-r0 to 2.29.1-r1, x86_64 and aarch64; 2.6.4-r0 is published for aarch64 only). Builds before 2.27.1-r1 contain Go programs and no Rust code. From 2.27.1-r1 on (2.27.1-r1 to 2.29.1-r1), each build bundles uv 0.13.6 at /opt/docker/dhi/uv, and the crate list that cargo-auditable embeds in that binary, read for every one of those builds on both architectures, includes rsa 0.9.10, pulled in by the reqsign request-signing crates (reqsign-core, reqsign-google and reqsign-azure-storage). No published build carries rsa 0.10.0 or later, so every build from 2.27.1-r1 on is affected and none is fixed yet.
